Answer: D
Reason: The imaging series demonstrates a rapid progression from initial interstitial opacities to severe bilateral alveolar consolidations, followed by complete resolution in the follow-up X-rays (Figures 5a and 5b). This pattern of acute lung injury with full radiological recovery is characteristic of Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis) pulmonary involvement, distinguishing it from conditions like Goodpasture syndrome or bacterial pneumonia which typically leave residual fibrosis or resolve differently.
